newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican gov't to allow U.S. cherry imports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican gov't to allow U.S. cherry imports.

text.p: Mexico and the United States signed an agreement Thursday to allow U.S. cherry exports to enter Mexico, the Agriculture Ministry said in a statement.
The accord follows six years of negotiations to establish phytosanitary requirements for the fruit, which will be exported from the states of California, Oregon and Washington.
Mexico's Agriculture ministry said these states have the least disease risk.
Cherries are rarely seen in Mexico, and the ministry said the volume of imports will depend on demand in a relatively new market.
"These imports, in any case, will not displace any Mexican producer, given that the fruit is not produced in the country for commercial reasons," the statement said.
The agreement was signed by the ministry and representatives from the USDA, and can be annuled if phytosanitary conditions are not followed, the statement said.
